events.title: The eleven buried at Muileann chrom
events.body: The eleven dead of the fall at Cnoc fhiadhaich are buried in the ground above the mill at Muileann chrom on the fourth day after the fall. Marsaili nic Sheumais, keeper of the old cutting for Taigh na Fèithe, reads their names at the graves and writes each into the roll with father, mother and hearth, and the place as under the wild hill.

events.title: Old Dòmhnall says the words at the pit-mouth
events.body: When the eleven are brought out of the fallen heading at Cnoc fhiadhaich, Dòmhnall, an old hewer of the custodians' cutting and father of Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, says the words of the face at the mouth of the drift, and the old hewers take them up. They had not been said at that pit-mouth since it was opened.

events.title: The fallen heading cleared and timbered
events.body: The fall at Cnoc fhiadhaich is cleared by midsummer and the heading timbered pair by pair as it is cleared, with oak brought up from Cathair fhada in an t-Ògmhios. The crews are paid nothing for the days of digging, and the yield of the year is short.

events.title: Raghnall asks three times for timber at the heading
events.body: Between an Gearran and an Giblean the crew-leaders Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill and Ailean mac Dhùghaill ask the agent at Cnoc fhiadhaich three times for props over the heading, where the shale roof has turned the colour the hewers read as bad ground. The agent writes the asking in his book and answers that oak will come in the summer.

events.title: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill at the pit-mouth
events.body: Dòmhnall, the six-year-old son of the crew-leader Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, who had gone to the breakers' benches at Muileann chrom in the autumn, takes An Casad Tioram in am Màrt. He coughs nine nights on his father's knee and wakes well on the tenth morning, and goes back to the benches in the autumn.

events.title: The custodians ask that the breakers' benches be shut
events.body: With An Casad Tioram running through the summer among the children who break coal, the custodians of Taigh na Fèithe ask the agent of A' Chompanaidh to shut the benches at Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich until it has passed. He writes the asking in his book, and the benches stay open to feed the pump furnaces.

events.title: The hill crews go home to the harvest
events.body: At the harvests after the fall and after An Casad Tioram the crews of Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich go home to their oats, a third of them the first year and half the second, and many stay home through the autumn. The yield of A' Chompanaidh in the hills falls short three years together.

events.title: The orphans carried to Cill thais
events.body: In an t-Iuchar Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill drives fourteen orphans of the fall and An Casad Tioram in a borrowed cart from Muileann chrom to Cill thais, two days west, with the crate of primers sent by A' Chompanaidh. The warden of Cill thais lifts each child down, has their names written, and sets the crate on a shelf of Taigh nan Dìlleachdan.

events.title: Hill coal burned for the lime of Baile ìseal
events.body: The lime for the mortar of the tower at Baile ìseal is burned in a kiln on the shore with coal carted over the hills from Muileann chrom. The tower is built by the masons of the eastern coast of the grey stone of the cape, with a lamp sent by A' Chompanaidh.

events.title: The fishing families of Baile ìseal draw lots for the watches
events.body: At the custodians' asking, the keeping of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal is given to the fishing households that had kept the driftwood fire on the cape. They draw lots for the watches at Samhain as they had drawn them for the fire, and the old fire is still lit beside the tower.

events.title: Torcall Clachair's last cairn
events.body: Going home west from Baile ìseal in the spring after the lighting, Torcall Clachair has his cart stopped where the road tops the first rise of the moor and the tower first shows over the heather. Seated by the road, he lays a small cairn with his own hands from stones a boy brings from the ditch. He builds no more.

events.title: Raghnall takes the leader's share
events.body: The agent at Cnoc fhiadhaich offers Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a leader's share on every ton his three crews raise, paid to him alone, if he keeps them at the face through harvest and winter; otherwise men of the coast will be brought up. Raghnall puts his mark to the paper in an Cèitean and keeps his crews below through the harvest.

events.title: Men of the foreshores shipped to Ceann òg
events.body: In the autumn A' Chompanaidh gathers fishers and net-menders whose foreshores it has bought, ships them from the capital's quays in the traders' boats of Seòlaid Ceann òg round the western capes and up the Abhainn ìseal to Ceann òg, and walks them over the hills to the workings in companies of twenty with their families.

events.title: The first crews in the huts at Àth ìseal
events.body: The first companies from the coast move into the plank huts at Àth ìseal, three long huts with a stove in each, a store and a well, with more rows pegged out beyond. The roll of Taigh na Fèithe notes that the camp has no custodian and has asked for none.

events.title: Beathag Dhubh asks for the order at Cnoc fhiadhaich
events.body: Beathag Dhubh, custodian of Doire mhòr, goes down to the washing-floors at Cnoc fhiadhaich with the carter Seònaid Bhàn and asks the agent Amos Tanner to show her the order that took her village's stream. He has none. The washing needs water, he says, and the stream goes with the working; a complaint may be written and sent on to Ros dhomhain.

events.title: Doire mhòr carries its water from the cattle spring
events.body: With the stream penned behind the washing gang's bank, the households of Doire mhòr carry their water by yoke and pail from the cattle spring at the foot of the brae, the better part of a mile each way. Beathag Dhubh's roll names every household that carries, and among the carriers is Tormod, son of Ruairidh.

events.title: Beathag Dhubh's letter to the council entered
events.body: The custodian of Doire mhòr writes to Comhairle a' Chùraim at Cathair dhearg of the taking of Doire mhòr's stream. Seònaid Bhàn carries the letter down the road in her cart and puts it into the hand of a custodians' clerk. The council enters it in its roll, and the stream is not let go that season.

events.title: Muireall carries Gormshuil's papers to the loft at Muileann chaol
events.body: Muireall nic Fhearchair drives her aunt Gormshuil's papers east in a hired pony-cart to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol, away from the reach of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir. Held by rain at Cuan chrom, she reads Clàr nan Dà Fhichead Dath aloud to the carter Seònaid Bhàn.

events.title: The store at Àth ìseal takes no barter
events.body: In the hungry autumn the store of A' Chompanaidh at Àth ìseal sells meal to the hill villages over its counter for marks only. Its clerk refuses cheese, wool and a woman's bronze brooch, having no book for them, and the women of the villages send their men back to the pits for coin.

events.title: The meal-carts of Doire fhiadhaich lodged at Cuan chrom
events.body: Nine ox-carts of meal from the villages of Doire fhiadhaich, sent north to the hungry hills under Lagh a' Bhìdh Roinnte, reach the ford at Cuan chrom in the rain of an Dàmhair. The carter of Cuan chrom, Seònaid Bhàn's father, takes their drivers and oxen into his own house and byre for the night.

events.title: Seven carts give their meal at the village doors
events.body: Of the nine meal-carts from Doire fhiadhaich, the seven that refuse the agents' marks at Àth ìseal go on into the hills and give their meal away sack by sack at the doors of the hill villages, as Lagh a' Bhìdh Roinnte bids. Their drivers come home by the carriers' road with empty carts.

events.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg
events.body: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg in the last days of an t-Sultain, in her seventy-first year. She had kept the council's list of the island's words since the ships came, refused to sign Puingean a' Chalaidh, and learned the humans' letters in her old age.

events.title: The first households leave Doire mhòr
events.body: In the second summer of the carrying the first households of Doire mhòr leave the village. Most go down to the timber huts at Àth ìseal, others to Muileann chrom or the capital. Tormod, who had carried water up for two summers, goes down to Àth ìseal with the rest. Beathag Dhubh stays.

events.title: The shrine-stone of Cidhe Beag set under a rowan
events.body: When the canoe landing at Cidhe Beag is widened into a coal quay, the old ferryman of the landing chooses a new place for its shrine-stone on the bank above, under a rowan within sight of the water. Four masons carry it up on a hurdle, and the ferryman puts meal in its hollow.

events.title: The last salmon netted at the green river's mouth
events.body: The fishermen of Ceann leathan net the last salmon taken at the mouth of the Abhainn uaine, a small hen fish found empty of eggs. The next spring no fish come in from the sea, the gravel of their spawning grounds lying under the grey slurry from the washing-floors.

events.title: Seònaid Bhàn marries Pàdraig mac Artair
events.body: Seònaid Bhàn, carter of Cuan chrom, marries Pàdraig mac Artair, a carter of Doire chaol. They live in her father's house at Cuan chrom beside the roofless carters' house at the quay, and their son Murchadh is born there the next winter.

events.title: Seònaid Bhàn takes the old carters' house at Cuan chrom
events.body: The custodians of Cuan chrom let the roofless carters' house at their quay to Seònaid Bhàn for a rent of one cheese a year. Twenty carters of Doire chaol give a week's work each towards the new roof for a year's lodging at half price, and its timber comes up from Doire fhiadhaich.

events.title: Seònaid's rule of marks and barter
events.body: On the first night of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr Seònaid Bhàn takes a hill carter's cheese and fleece for his bed and supper at the same rate as marks. She has the rule cut on a board over the eastern hearth in the old strokes: Bonn no bathar, an aon bhobhla, coin or goods, the same bowl.

events.title: The carters of Doire chaol swear at Seònaid's table
events.body: Through the winter some thirty carters of Doire chaol, Cuan chrom and the capital meet at the eastern hearth of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr over the lowered rate for hauling coal. On Pàdraig mac Artair's counsel they swear, with their hands on the board of Seònaid's rule, to go to Ros dhomhain together and haul nothing at the new rate.

events.title: Amos Tanner bargains with the carters at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr
events.body: Amos Tanner, agent of A' Chompanaidh for the carriage of coal, rides up Rathad na Mèinne to meet the carters' guild of Doire chaol at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr. He tells them of the new coal stage at Seann Toll and the lesser hauling on the road, and they bargain over the rate into the night.

events.title: A coal ship runs down a Ceann leathan boat
events.body: A coal ship of A' Chompanaidh coming out of the river mouth on the ebb runs down a fishing boat of Ceann leathan off the bar and does not stop. The two men aboard are taken from the water alive by their neighbours. Within a season the town's boats keep inshore of the ships' track and lie to at the bar when a hull comes down.

events.title: Enoch Pratt offers Raghnall the staff
events.body: In an Cèitean Enoch Pratt, agent of A' Chompanaidh at the pits of Muileann chrom, offers Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a staff of ash capped with brass, a weekly wage in marks and a house, to be set over all the crews of the hill and answer for them to the agent. Raghnall, forty-six years old, takes it.

events.title: Raghnall's slate-roofed house
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's masons from Ros dhomhain build Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a house of two rooms and a loft on common grazing above the mill at Muileann chrom, with glass windows and a roof of slate, the first slate roof in the town. The miller's wife names him Raghnall Maor as he goes by, and the crews take up the name.

events.title: The roll of Taigh na Fèithe stops naming the overseers
events.body: Marsaili nic Sheumais, who keeps the roll of Taigh na Fèithe, enters the first four overseers of the hill by name, then puts the matter to the custodians of the vein. From then on the roll gives only their number under the date, seven in the first year, and says of them only that several are hawk-faithful.

events.title: Seumas Dubh set over the pits at Cnoc mhòr
events.body: When A' Chompanaidh opens new pits at Cnoc mhòr and asks for an overseer, Raghnall Maor gives the name of Seumas Dubh, who came into his crews at fifteen. Seumas takes the staff and goes south with his household to a crew of Cnoc mhòr men new to the seam, and runs the haulage three tubs to the rope.

events.title: Coinneach Beag crushed on the haulage
events.body: The haulage rope at Cnoc mhòr parts under three full tubs, and the tubs run back into the gallery-mouth and crush Coinneach Beag, a boy of eleven coming up the rails with an empty. The custodians' roll of Cnoc mhòr gives his name, his age and his mother's name; A' Chompanaidh's report gives the cost of the rope.

events.title: The two hanged named in the custodians' roll
events.body: The roll of Cnoc mhòr names the two hewers hanged at Ros dhomhain for the killing of Seumas Dubh, Eòin Ruadh and Fionnlagh mac Aonghais, and records that their neighbours carried them home and buried them in the town's ground. The letter-book of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir gives them as two of the crew.

events.title: The overseers made to stand at the hanging
events.body: By Henry Maddox's order every overseer of the island stands in a row in front of the crowd at the hanging at Ros dhomhain, fourteen men with their staffs, inside a square of the soldiers of Riaghaltas nan Coigreach. The custodians' roll of Ros dhomhain enters in a line of its own that the overseers stood in front.

events.title: A staff left at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr
events.body: Riding home from the hanging, an overseer of Àth ìseal leaves his staff against the wall of Seònaid Bhàn's house at the half-way stage of Rathad na Mèinne, and in the morning it is gone. He tells the agent it is lost, and A' Chompanaidh gives him another.

events.title: The sermon in the road at Àth ìseal
events.body: Turned back at the gate of the camp at Àth ìseal under Maddox's order by the hawk-faithful overseer Iomhar Bàn, an old priest of Òrd an t-Seabhaig sits down in the road outside the fence, and the crews come out to hear him there. When he is done Iomhar kneels in the road for his blessing. Raghnall Maor stands by.

events.title: The pox dead of the hill buried below Achadh dhomhain
events.body: A' Bhreac Bhallach comes up Rathad na Mèinne into the camps of the hill in the last days of an Dàmhair, worst at Àth ìseal and Achadh dhomhain. A' Chompanaidh keeps the pits working. The custodians will not let the pox dead lie among the old graves, and the crews bury them by lamplight in new ground below Achadh dhomhain.

events.title: The custodians write their dead into the chaplains' margin
events.body: Marsaili nic Sheumais goes from hearth to hearth on the hill in the spring and writes down the pox dead the chaplains had not found. The custodians borrow the chaplains' list, write their own names down both margins in the old letters with the total at the foot, and send it back to Ros dhomhain, where it is filed.

events.title: The hill buries Beathag Dhubh
events.body: Some hundreds come up to Doire mhòr for Beathag Dhubh's burying, crews from the galleries unwashed among them, leaving A' Chompanaidh's cart-road at the bend to cross her fields by the old path. Raghnall Maor comes without his staff and stands at the back. The roll of Taigh na Fèithe writes her the last door of Doire mhòr that did not open.

events.title: Maddox's goods carried down to the ships
events.body: For a week A' Chompanaidh's carts go down Rathad na Mèinne to Ros dhomhain with Henry Maddox's goods, a tall clock lashed upright in a cart of its own among them, and all go aboard the ship that brought Arthur Lisle. The carters say that he came out with one chest.

events.title: Beathag Dhubh dies at Doire mhòr
events.body: Beathag Dhubh, custodian of Doire mhòr, who sent A' Chompanaidh's agent down the hill, dies in her own house in an Giblean at sixty-one, among the few hearths left lit after the stream was taken. She is laid out with Doire mhòr's own coal at her head and feet, and the whole hill comes up to her.

events.title: Lisle's rider gathers the papers of the hill
events.body: Under Arthur Lisle's first order a rider of Riaghaltas nan Coigreach takes the papers of the pits at Muileann chrom down to Ros dhomhain: the contract of the first thirty and the paper of Raghnall's leader's share. Asked for the agreement that gave the overseers their staffs, Enoch Pratt finds that there is none.
